## Plan summary

Re-point five prose-pin assertions from the repo-root always-on doc at the four
`.claude/rules/*.md` files that now carry the relocated prose. Single cause:
compaction commit 40653b5dcfb07588948d3ae9c896390691d17cc2 (2026-08-06) moved
four prose blocks out to cut always-on context load, and the pins were not
followed. Three nodes fail on assertion, two raise `ValueError: substring not
found` because the rung marker their window slices to no longer exists in the
always-on summary. Reproduced red at main 9c509772a0c13d4772955b5dfd0ff306b295f70d
(5 failed in 0.81s).

Pattern is the landed precedent 7163b0fea796a443aac9f99614f8ea375bd1d96f (#2159,
same compaction commit, same class): name the rule file in a module-level
constant, cite the compaction commit in a comment, swap the read target, keep
every window / ordering / count assertion byte-identical, do not rename the test
node. No prose returns to the always-on doc — the Goal forbids it.

The one substantive design call, resolved by evidence rather than preference: a
`count >= 2` assertion over a two-site contract. Both sites survived the
compaction but now live one per file, so the count is summed ACROSS both files
(acceptance-criteria option (a)) and each per-line token assertion is resolved
against whichever file now carries that line. The count is not weakened and no
site is dropped. Verified: each locator header hits exactly one line in its own
file, and every same-line token is present on that line.

No compaction content loss: every pinned string was located verbatim in exactly
one file before any re-point was designed, so the acceptance criteria's
report-do-not-weaken branch does not fire. The implementer re-verifies in-branch
and must honor that branch if any string turns out absent everywhere.
